newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Paranapanema lower in afternoon trade.
newsitem.headline: Paranapanema lower in afternoon trade.

text.p: Preferred shares of Brazil's Paranapanema were 8.1 percent lower at 10.20 reais in late afternoon trade despite the firm's statement clarifying news about a delay in a debenture payment, brokers said.

Paranapanema today published a statement saying that a delay in the payment of interest on convertible debentures it issued last year had been agreed with BNDESPar, which holds the paper. The statement was made necessary after Gazeta Mercantil financial newspaper on Wednesday suggested that Paranapanema had to delay the payment due to a fragile financial situation.
"This fact has nothing to do with financial difficulties," the company said in the published statement.

Earlier this month Paranapanema had to pay around 14 million reais in interest to BNDES Participacoes (BNDESPar), the investment arm of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), which acquired some 150 million reais in the firm's convertible debentures.

A total of 390 million reais in debentures convertible to voting shares were issued by Paranapanema after local pension funds acquired control of the firm and another three mining firms to form a mining conglomerate last year.
The pension funds and BNDESPar acquired the debentures but BNDESPar decided to hold onto the debentures instead of converting them into shares.

Paranapanema and BNDESPar agreed to postpone the deadline for the payment of interest on the debentures, said Helio Blak, the firm's Financial and Market Relations director. Under the agreement, Paranapanema would issue preferred shares which would be in part acquired by BNDESPar by using the debentures to pay for the shares.
No BNDESPar officials were immediately available to comment on the matter.
In the last two sessions, Paranapanema shares fell over ten percent, traders said.
Traders noted another factor behind the drop was the fact that the report also suggested that Paranapanema's majority shareholders were dissatisfied with the firm's management.
Paranapanema group was formed by mining firms Companhia Paraibuna de Metais, Caraiba Metais, Eluma and Mamore (formerly known as Paranapanema).
